title: Solar Vehicle
blurb:
Dynamics subteam member
Designed an 8-axis spoke with a 16.8% improvement over the previous design
about:
• Evaluated multiple wheel spoke geometries in SolidWorks and selected an eight-spoke 6061-T6 aluminum design to improve
load distribution while minimizing mass
• Derived a 1,558 N bump load and 169 Nm braking torque from vehicle weight and 2g vertical/1g longitudinal acceleration
conditions; validated structural performance using static FEA, mesh convergence, and hand calculations
• Reduced modeled wheel spoke mass by 16.8% (698 g to 581 g) compared to the previous year’s design while achieving
FEA-predicted factors of safety of 1.6 under bump loading and 3.9 under braking
organization: Cal Solar Vehicle Competition - Gen XII

title: Payload Design
blurb: A tethered weather-balloon system mapping vertical air-quality profiles up to 300 m, with a custom 3D-printed sensor payload.
about: This project involved designing and developing a tethered weather-balloon payload to collect air-quality measurements at altitudes up to 300 meters. As the mechanical design lead of a five-person team, I focused on creating a lightweight, structurally reliable enclosure that could safely house the electronics and sensors. Using Fusion 360, I performed finite element analysis (FEA) and shape optimization, reducing payload mass by 25.9% (from 353 g to 261 g) to lower helium requirements. I also developed CAD models, engineering drawings, and a Bill of Materials to support fabrication and assembly. I validated the final design through 20 N tether-load testing with no measured deformation, plus electronics fit checks and sensor functionality testing.

title: 2-Axis Gimbal
blurb: A 3-axis motorized gimbal that detects and tracks objects in real time — a CAD-designed mechanism paired with a YOLOv8 vision pipeline.
about: A three-axis motorized gimbal designed to keep a detected object centered in frame. The mechanical structure and joints were designed from first principles in Statics, then prototyped and refined in Fusion 360.
On the software side, the platform runs a YOLOv8 object-detection algorithm on a Raspberry Pi to locate targets, feeding the gimbal so the camera tracks motion autonomously.

title: Folding Knife
blurb: A back-lock folding knife designed in SolidWorks from A2 tool steel, heat-treated to a 273% increase in hardness.
about: A back-lock folding knife designed and prototyped in SolidWorks using A2 tool steel, with the design focused on the locking mechanism and the blade’s load paths.
By evaluating material behavior and load paths and applying precise heat treatment, I achieved a 273% increase in material hardness over the untreated stock.

title: Microfabrication
blurb: Wafer-based microstructure fabrication at UCLA’s California NanoSystems Institute — photolithography through wet etching, tuned for repeatability.
about: At UCLA’s California NanoSystems Institute, I manufactured wafer-based microstructures in a cleanroom using photolithography, electron-beam lithography, thin-film deposition, and wet chemical etching.
I optimized fabrication workflows by adjusting resist thickness and exposure parameters, maximizing pattern fidelity and process repeatability across runs.

title: Robotic Swarm
blurb: Mechanical and systems research for a NASA proposal built around a decentralized robotic swarm, mapped to NASA taxonomy TX04.
about: As Mechanical Researcher on an interdisciplinary L’SPACE team, I helped develop a NASA proposal centered on a decentralized robotic swarm. I directed research against system-level requirements spanning mechanical hardware (wheels, chassis), thermal control, power, and communications.

We collaborated with subject-matter experts to ground the proposal in NASA taxonomy TX04 (Robotics and Autonomous Systems), translating mission objectives into concrete mechanical and systems constraints.

title: Posture Pack
blurb: A posture-tracking device built at the Cal Poly Pomona Hackathon — custom enclosure, embedded sensing, and a React/TypeScript feedback dashboard.
about: Posture Pack is a posture-tracking device prototyped at the Cal Poly Pomona Hackathon to help students keep proper posture while studying. I CAD-modeled a custom housing to integrate a Raspberry Pi, breadboard, and distance sensor.
On the software side, I built a React/TypeScript interface to collect, display, and model posture data, giving users real-time feedback on their position.

title: CX-5 Telemetry
blurb: MATLAB modeling of vehicle OBD telemetry — position, velocity, acceleration, RPM, and fuel rate over time.
about: Using MATLAB, I analyzed telemetry from a Mazda CX-5, modeling position, velocity, acceleration, RPM, and fuel rate over time.
From raw OBD-II sensor data I built mathematical models and visualizations to evaluate engine and drivetrain behavior across driving conditions.
